changed.what: KA-844 (reality of a certified root) is N38-KA's record and derivation file. Its entry `ka:KA-844@host|auditor` and its control, plant `N38b-45:cx-393`, belong to N38b-45, which depends on this bead (N38b-45 -> N25d-23 -> N10c-05). The bead claimed to write the row's derivation file, attach its control and bind the number. Its e2e ran `g1_known_answers -- KA-844` with `reality_from_real_part` required to fail the row. Left as it was, the implementer would write a second derivation file and control for a row N38-KA already defines. The e2e step could never pass at this bead's acceptance, because the entry it runs comes from a bead that waits on this one. Changes: Scope, section 5 and acceptance now say the law test `reality_robust_test` reproduces KA-844 on the reference model and that the bead adds no row, number, derivation file or control. The e2e drops the KA-844 g1 run; instead it runs the mutant as a law-suite subject and checks the registry for KA-844's record with control `N38b-45:cx-393`. Table row: tier corrected to `G1 host, auditor` as N38-KA has it, and the control is named as N38b-45's plant, with `reality_from_real_part` as this bead's law-suite mutant.

Step 3c ran each law suite with `--features controls`. BD-025 defines no such feature, so cargo refuses the build. As written, step 3c fails for every construction and `--milestone M1` can never exit 0, or the implementer invents a feature that BD-025 and N10a-01 section 6 rule out. Step 3c now uses the form of N10a-01 section 6, the same as sibling N10a-22: one build per registered control, with the feature the control's record names. That is `cargo test -p <crate> --features <feature> --test <target>` in an owning crate, or `--features gauntlet-mutations,<feature>` while the suite is staged in frob-conformance. The test named in the record must fail, and `controls_are_caught` runs in each build. Also, the paragraph on further rows and provisional tags said those checks happen at 'step 2d'. Step 2 is the doctrine test, and the acceptance criterion requires `provisional-tag-past-due` at step 3d. Both references now read 3d, so the log's `step` field matches the acceptance check.

KA-845 (the Cayley map on SE(3)) is N38-KA's record and derivation file. N38b-39 (M0) owns its entry `ka:KA-845@host`, binds the row by name (`ka_845_...`) and owns its control, the feature `frob-lie/cx-394` seeded from CX-394. N38-KA's row names the control `N38b-39:cx-394`. This bead instead bound KA-845 to its own test `cayley_se3_worked` 'with its derivation file' and named its control as the mutant `translation_unchanged`. Left as it was, the M1 implementer would rebind a row that N38b-39 bound at M0 and add a second control. That breaks N38b-39's acceptance, or the registry ends up with two bindings and two controls for one row. Changes: Scope, section 5 and acceptance now say that `cayley_se3_worked` reproduces KA-845 on the reference model, that `translation_unchanged` (a law-suite mutant) fails it, and that the bead adds no row, number, derivation file or control. The KA-845 table row names the plant `N38b-39:cx-394`. The e2e no longer runs `g1_known_answers -- KA-845`: that entry is N38b-39's, and depending on N38b-39 would pull in BD-011, which this bead states it does not depend on. Instead the e2e runs the mutant as a law-suite subject and checks the registry for KA-845's record and control.

Convention 13. The register row's `verb` was described as routed through `mission.refute` 'until the M4 verbs are registered', with a possible rename. VERBS-mission already registers `--baseline`, `--baseline-policy` and `--paired-plan` on the `mission.refute` row from M4 for BD-359's product-system dominance, and BD-359's script uses that form. Left as it was, the implementer would fill row C-40's verb as a provisional placeholder and might wait for a dominance verb that no registry will add. The row now states the registered form as a fact.
